newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian police mull senator claims - source.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian police mull senator claims - source.

text.p: The Australian Federal Police are examining allegations against key independent senator Mal Colston but have not investigated their veracity, a government source said on Tuesday.
"They're looking at it," said the source, an official familiar with the operations of the federal police.
A former employee has accused Colston in an administrative tribunal of misusing an expense allowance and giving government-paid jobs in his office to relatives who did no work.
Colston, whose vote last year saved much of the government's deficit-slashing budget, denies the allegations and says he is suing the employee who made them.

The senator is one of two independents in the upper house of parliament. The pair routinely supply the two votes that the Liberal-National coalition government needs to get contentious legislation through the parliament.
All other non-government senators belong to leftist parties that usually oppose the conservative government's contentious measures.
The Australian constitution excludes people convicted of serious offences -- warranting a year's jail term or more -- from sitting in parliament.
